## Question

How does Donald Trump's rhetoric differ before, during, and after UCDP-recorded lethal conflict events in Iran with explicit U.S. involvement?

The U.S. involvement focus is deliberate. Joint U.S.–Israel events are kept, along with lethal incidents reported in a U.S. operation context. Records without a documented U.S. role in the reviewed evidence are withheld; this does not prove that the U.S. was uninvolved. This is a descriptive study of language around recorded conflict events. Advance warning is an exploratory hypothesis; the current evidence does not establish a reliable predictive signal.

## Data

The October 11, 2026 refresh aligns **49 UCDP Candidate records across 28 event start dates** with **90 unique matched posts (132 post/event pairs)**. All 47 records in the prior extract are retained. The August release adds **UCDP 640608, August 30 at Larak Island**, whose source headlines explicitly describe a U.S. attack; its best fatality estimate is 2 (low–high 2–3). The selection review also adds **UCDP 629301, April 5 in Boyer-Ahmad county**, reporting five deaths during the U.S. pilot-rescue operation. July 30 is now shown even though no posts match its windows.

**Why 49 records but 28 dates?** UCDP can record multiple events with the same start date. The timeline groups those records at one date point, so 49 records produce 28 distinct date points. No records are discarded in this grouping. For example, April 5 now contains the pilot-rescue record and a separate joint U.S.–Israel strike record in Ardebil. Multi-day records use their recorded start date as an anchor.

- **UCDP Candidate:** January–June version 26.01.26.06, July 26.0.7, and August 26.0.8. Inclusion requires an Iran record in conflict 16905 and reviewed evidence documenting U.S. or joint U.S.–Israel action, or a lethal incident reported during a U.S. operation. The combined Israel/U.S. dyad cannot establish U.S. involvement on its own. Candidate records are provisional.
- **Truth Social archive:** the [Cameronk199 public archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cameronk199/donald-trump-truth-social-posts), revision `eaeb102e183204635582de3eaae6c741cd383c32`. The original 87 reviewed posts are preserved; later original text posts matching Iran/Iranian, Tehran, Hormuz, or Khamenei extend the extract. Quote posts and reblogs are excluded. Attached images and videos are not classified.

Post timestamps and post-window membership use **America/New_York (EST/EDT)**. UCDP event dates remain source-coded calendar dates; no intraday event time is available, so a day-before post is not necessarily a full 24-hour lead. Events on adjacent dates can reuse the same post in different windows. Multi-day records appear as context at their start date without assigning their whole fatality total to that day.

The archive ends **August 31 at 08:09 EDT**. Its partial day-after window is displayed but excluded from the comparison. Empty windows are kept in the timeline and omitted from score averages; an absent post is not a zero score.

## UCDP source and selection

**What this source is:** the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) Candidate Events Dataset records lethal organized violence using event dates, locations, actor coding, fatality estimates, and cited source reports. Candidate records are provisional and can be revised.

**Why it is used here:** UCDP supplies documented event dates around which to group Trump's posts. The events are selected from UCDP independently of the rhetoric scores. This provides a consistent reference for comparing language before, on, and after recorded conflict events.

### Exact records used by the timeline

This second window contains **only the 49 selected UCDP records**, matching the timeline's CSV by persistent record ID. Their **28 event start dates** define the before/event-day/after post windows. Multiple records can share one start date, and a multi-day record can cover a longer interval. Record counts therefore do not represent independent intervention onsets, and multi-day fatality totals are not assigned to the first day.

July 30 is included as an event date even though it has no matched posts. The August release adds the U.S.-attributed August 30 Larak Island event, **UCDP 640608**. Use the release filter to view that August record directly.

**Pilot-rescue inclusion:** [the AFP report for UCDP 629301](https://www.thedailystar.net/news/world/us-israel-war-iran/news/five-killed-iran-strikes-during-us-pilot-rescue-iranian-media-4144001) links five reported deaths to the U.S. rescue operation. It does not explicitly identify the strike actor, so the project labels this record **U.S. operation context**. The official fields remain unchanged. Adding it changes April 5's selected same-day fatality total from 5 to 10 and the display category from Notable to High. April 5 was already a timeline date, so post windows and rhetoric averages are unchanged.

## Event activity levels

The central event circle and the clickable bottom timeline use the following display categories, based on UCDP fatality estimates and record counts. These thresholds are defined for this visualization; they are not UCDP classifications or tests of statistical significance.

<ul>
<li><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:#a7adb3;margin-right:8px;vertical-align:middle;"></span><strong>Minor:</strong> a same-day record below the Notable, High, and Major thresholds.</li>
<li><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:#69737d;margin-right:8px;vertical-align:middle;"></span><strong>Notable:</strong> same-day best estimate ≥ 5, or at least 2 same-day UCDP records.</li>
<li><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:#4f575f;margin-right:8px;vertical-align:middle;"></span><strong>High:</strong> same-day best estimate ≥ 10, or at least 3 same-day UCDP records.</li>
<li><span style="display:inline-block;width:15px;height:15px;border-radius:50%;background:#292f35;margin-right:8px;vertical-align:middle;"></span><strong>Major:</strong> same-day best death estimate ≥ 25, or same-day civilian deaths ≥ 10.</li>
<li><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:white;box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px #70777e;margin-right:8px;vertical-align:middle;"></span><strong>Multi-day Event:</strong> a multi-day record begins on that date, but there is no same-day fatality record to assign to that specific date.</li>
</ul>

The intent is to visually emphasize dates with more substantial same-day UCDP activity, without assigning an entire multi-day fatality total to the first day of a long record.

## Approach

1. **Collect** Trump's Truth Social posts from the archived snapshot and UCDP's Iran-conflict records from the versioned CSV releases. Apply the documented U.S.-involvement selection decisions.
2. **Window** the two datasets together: for every distinct UCDP event start date, pull Iran-related posts from the day before, day of, and day after.
3. **Score rhetoric with zero-shot classification.** A Hugging Face multi-label zero-shot classifier (`facebook/bart-large-mnli`) scores each post's `content_text` — and only the text, never the UCDP metadata — against six categories: **Threat, Victory, Diplomacy, Ceasefire/Ending, Blame Allies, and Media Criticism**, each receiving a continuous 0–1 entailment score.
4. **Aggregate means by event start date.** Average post scores within each date's window, then average those date means. Each date with matched posts contributes equally, so a high-volume posting day does not dominate the comparison.
5. **Visualize** each event start date at a central node sized and shaded by its activity level, with posts from before, on, and after that date branching around it. Each post also has a small colored badge for its highest-scoring category.


## Rhetorical category guide

The six categories are **multi-label**: the model evaluates each one independently, so a single post can score highly in more than one category. In computational text analysis these are often called rhetorical “frames,” but this page uses **category** as the plainer label. The values are model entailment scores, not calibrated probabilities.

Each card below is the **highest-scoring post for that category** among the original 87-post snapshot (these illustrative examples are retained from that snapshot). The full archived post is shown directly in the card, followed by that post's scores across all six categories and a link to the original Truth Social post.

### Diplomacy

Diplomacy, negotiations, talks, deals, conditions, agreements, or communication with Iran or allied governments.

### Ceasefire / Ending

A ceasefire, stopping military operations, ending the conflict, pausing attacks, or declaring the fighting essentially finished.

This same post is the highest-scoring example for both categories, which shows why the model is treated as multi-label rather than forcing each post into only one category.

## Results

<p><a href="assets/political-text-analysis/trump-iran-connected-timeline.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Open the timeline in its own full-width page ↗</a> — recommended on desktop, since the embed below is narrower than the page it's showing and falls back to the mobile layout.</p>

<div class="column-page" style="margin: 1.5rem 0;">
<iframe
  id="political-timeline-frame"
  title="Explore posts around U.S.-involved Iran events"
  src="assets/political-text-analysis/trump-iran-connected-timeline.html"
  style="width: 100%; height: 900px; border: 1px solid #444; border-radius: 8px;"
  loading="lazy">
</iframe>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  const frame = document.getElementById("political-timeline-frame");
  if (!frame) return;
  function cleanPoliticalTimelineChrome() {
    try {
      const doc = frame.contentDocument;
      if (!doc) return;
      const innerNav = doc.querySelector(".site-nav");
      if (innerNav) innerNav.style.setProperty("display", "none", "important");
      if (doc.body) doc.body.classList.remove("has-shared-nav");
    } catch (error) {}
  }
  frame.addEventListener("load", cleanPoliticalTimelineChrome);
  cleanPoliticalTimelineChrome();
})();
</script>

The timeline groups posts around each UCDP event start date and shows their scores for Threat, Victory, Diplomacy, Ceasefire/Ending, Blame Allies, and Media Criticism. A small badge identifies each post's highest-scoring category. The summary compares average scores across the before, event-day, and after windows, giving each date with posts equal weight. On narrow screens, use the tabs to switch between windows; on wider screens, the three windows appear side by side.

**Descriptive findings:** Victory framing is prominent across the sampled windows, with mean scores of 0.688 before, 0.769 on the event day, and 0.700 after. Threat scores average 0.558 before, 0.505 on the event day, and 0.485 after. These are model entailment scores, not probabilities of a military event. Each column averages only dates with posts in that window: 21 before, 22 on the event day, and 21 after.

Comparing the same event dates shows how sensitive the apparent day-before Threat increase is to the available sample:

::: {.selection-table-window role="region" tabindex="0" aria-label="Threat comparison; scroll horizontally on narrow screens"}

| Threat comparison | Event dates | Before | Event day |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Posts available before and on the event day | 18 | 0.571 | 0.503 |
| Posts available in all three windows | 14 | 0.579 | 0.594 |

:::

The paired before-minus-event-day difference is +0.068. An exploratory 95% interval from resampling chronological episodes spans approximately −0.166 to +0.352, including no difference. Episodes join event dates no more than three days apart; only eight episodes contribute to this comparison. Requiring all three windows changes the sample and removes the day-before advantage. This sensitivity check does not correct missingness. The evidence supports describing rhetoric around events, while the advance-warning hypothesis remains inconclusive. [Inspect the numerical checks](assets/political-text-analysis/indicator-check.json).

## Further research: testing advance warning

1. Use only posts available before the outcome date. Keep event-day and day-after language as context, not advance predictors.
2. Compare the day-before signal with comparable days during the same conflict on which no qualifying U.S.-involved event is recorded. "No UCDP record" is not proof that no operation occurred.
3. Define the flag and horizon on an earlier development period, then evaluate on later held-out dates. Report false alarms, missed events, precision, recall, and the underlying event rate.
4. Account for clustered event dates and repeated posts; separate new intervention onsets from follow-on actions during ongoing operations. Sensitivity checks should exclude imprecisely dated and multi-day anchors.
5. Audit classifier labels by hand. The current Threat description includes both warnings and reports of completed strikes, and some non-threat language can receive a high score. Text-only scores also miss signals carried in attached media.

## Limitations

- **Selected sample:** 90 unique posts and 28 start dates in one leader's rhetoric during one conflict. Empty windows are visible but have no rhetoric score. The original post selection was reviewed manually and is preserved, so this is not a fresh exhaustive classification of the full archive.
- **No non-event baseline or held-out warning evaluation yet.** This is an exploratory timeline, not an operational prediction tool.
- **Unequal denominators and overlapping windows:** before/day-of/after means are not a paired independent sample. Several dates can share the same post; a previous-day post may be reacting to an earlier strike.
- **Provisional event timing and attribution:** UCDP Candidate records can be revised. Source-coded dates lack intraday timing; shared dyad coding alone does not identify the attacker.
- **Event-selection coverage:** the current review checks supplied headline/source fields for all 80 Iran-conflict records, with two full AFP reports additionally checked. The 31 withheld records are not proven Israel-only. Further source review could establish U.S. involvement and expand the sample. The rescue record documents U.S. operation context with the strike actor unspecified.
- **Fatality-based inclusion:** the event set does not cover every military operation, diplomatic moment, sanction, or negotiation.
- **Model scores:** BART entailment scores are uncalibrated and heuristic, not probabilities of intervention or validated measures of intent. The classifier is not fine-tuned for this domain.
- **Snapshot coverage:** August 31 is incomplete in the post archive, and later UCDP months are not part of the latest listed August release.

## References and downloads

### Full official UCDP CSVs

The following downloads are unmodified global UCDP Candidate files. The 80-record source viewer and 49-record timeline CSV are project extracts from these releases.

- **[Full January–June 2026 CSV](assets/political-text-analysis/ucdp-official/GEDEvent_v26_01_26_06.csv):** version 26.01.26.06; 10,051 global records. [Original at UCDP ↗](https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/candidateged/GEDEvent_v26_01_26_06.csv).
- **[Full July 2026 CSV](assets/political-text-analysis/ucdp-official/GEDEvent_v26_0_7.csv):** version 26.0.7; 1,828 global records. [Original at UCDP ↗](https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/candidateged/GEDEvent_v26_0_7.csv).
- **[Full August 2026 CSV](assets/political-text-analysis/ucdp-official/GEDEvent_v26_0_8.csv):** version 26.0.8; 1,806 global records. [Original at UCDP ↗](https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/candidateged/GEDEvent_v26_0_8.csv).

[UCDP official Candidate releases and codebook ↗](https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/)

Please cite UCDP Candidate as: Hegre, Håvard, Mihai Croicu, Kristine Eck, and Stina Högbladh (2020), *Introducing the UCDP Candidate Events Dataset*, Research & Politics.

### How the reference files were narrowed

::: {.selection-table-window role="region" tabindex="0" aria-label="Selection steps; scroll horizontally on narrow screens"}

| Stage | Kept | What was cut and why |
|:--|--:|:--|
| Full January–August releases | 13,685 source rows | Worldwide starting files, before any project filter. |
| Country: Iran | 172 records | 13,513 rows coded to other countries; this study covers events located in Iran. |
| Iran–Israel/U.S. conflict (`conflict_new_id = 16905`) | 80 records | 92 Iran records in other UCDP conflicts; they fall outside this study's conflict scope. |
| Documented U.S. involvement | 49 records | 31 records whose reviewed evidence does not establish a U.S. role. Joint U.S.–Israel action and the U.S. pilot-rescue context are kept. |
| Group by recorded start date | 28 date groups | No further exclusions. Multiple records with the same start date share one clickable point. |

:::

The three global files contain 13,685 rows and 13,659 distinct UCDP IDs. The 26 repeated IDs are outside the Iran subset; all 172 Iran records have distinct IDs. Iran contributes 121 records from January–June, 39 from July, and 12 from August. The conflict filter retains 59, 20, and 1 respectively.

**Why the selected count changed from 48 to 49:** the original 47 records and the August 30 Larak Island record were preserved in the initial refresh. The subsequent review restored **UCDP 629301**, reporting five deaths during the U.S. pilot-rescue operation on April 5. The revised selection contains **26 joint U.S.–Israel records, 22 U.S.-attributed records, and 1 U.S. operation-context record**. This is a documented selected sample, not a claim that every U.S.-involved incident has been identified.

#### Why 31 records are withheld

::: {.selection-table-window role="region" tabindex="0" aria-label="Withheld record breakdown; scroll horizontally on narrow screens"}

| Current selection basis | Records | Why withheld |
|:--|--:|:--|
| Explicit Israeli attribution | 9 | The supplied headlines identify Israeli action without documenting a U.S. role. |
| U.S. role unverified in the other reviewed records | 22 | 17 do not establish U.S. participation, 3 mention U.S. officials, sanctions, or warnings without linking the U.S. to the incident, 1 combines Trump's comment with an Israeli strike claim, and 1 concerns Iranian demining deaths without establishing the ordnance's origin. |

:::

**Unverified does not mean absent.** The original exclusion rationales were not logged. These are the current October 11 decisions based on the evidence actually reviewed, rather than invented historical explanations. All 80 supplied headline/source fields were checked; full AFP articles were additionally checked for the rescue record and UCDP 629300. Other full articles remain to be reviewed if stronger U.S. attribution is needed.

Run `python scripts/build_ucdp_references.py` to rebuild the two reference viewers' data from the frozen source-pool and used-record extracts. To reconstruct the source pool from the three official CSV downloads, pass `--source-dir PATH`; their recorded checksums must match.
